book_title: Chapter 3: The Global Fab Network, Supply Chain & Unit Economics
question: How does TSMC allocate capacity, manage its equipment supply chain, and turn $100 of sales into $59.89 of gross profit and $26.32 of free cash flow?

epigraph.quote: Every leading-edge wafer is co-engineered years before a single mask is printed.
epigraph.author: TSMC Open Innovation Platform Principles

web_blocks.text: Go-To-Market: Direct Engineering, OIP & Capacity Prepayments

web_blocks.html: TSMC uses zero distributors or middlemen for its leading-edge foundry business. Sales run through direct, multi-year engineering work between TSMC field engineers and client chip teams, anchored by the Open Innovation Platform (OIP) [1]. OIP certifies Process Design Kits (PDKs), EDA tools (Synopsys, Cadence, Siemens EDA), and core IP blocks (Arm, Synopsys) years before tape-out. Porting a 3nm or 2nm chip to a rival foundry means re-verifying billions of transistors. Thus, OIP creates high switching friction before a client orders its first production wafer.

To de-risk $20 billion+ GigaFab builds, TSMC pairs direct engineering with multi-year capacity deals, long-term agreements (LTAs), and client prepayments. Cloud giants and top fabless designers lock in wafer banks and CoWoS slots 12 to 24 months ahead. They often post non-refundable deposits or take-or-pay volume minimums. This model kept Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) tight at 27.0 days in FY2025, down from 34.3 days in FY2024. Meanwhile, Days of Inventory Outstanding (DIO) fell from 82.7 days to 68.8 days [16].

web_blocks.takeaway: Taiwan remains the irreplaceable cost and yield anchor; overseas fabs solve geopolitical mandates at a 2%–4% consolidated gross margin headwind.

web_blocks.html: Upstream, TSMC buys from a tight equipment and materials oligopoly. ASML holds a 100% monopoly on Extreme Ultraviolet (EUV) and High-NA EUV scanners. Tokyo Electron, Applied Materials, and Lam Research supply etch, deposition, and track tools. Shin-Etsu Chemical and SUMCO lead in ultra-pure 300mm bare wafers and photoresists. TSMC cuts single-vendor risk through joint R&D, multi-year tool slots, and huge buying scale ($40.56B capex in FY2025, rising to $60B–$64B in FY2026) [1, 4].

web_blocks.title: Why Depreciation Is TSMC's Secret Cash Engine
paragraphs: Notice the $18.07 per $100 of depreciation in the FY2025 waterfall. TSMC depreciates fab tools fast—typically over 5 years—so GAAP gross margin understates true cash generation. Once a 5nm or 7nm fab passes its 5-year depreciation cliff, cash costs drop sharply while wafers still sell at healthy margins. That cash funds the next $60B+ capex wave without straining the balance sheet.

book_paragraphs: To see how a capital-heavy manufacturer acts like a software-margin compounder, examine TSMC's unit economics and sales model. There are no middlemen, no channel stuffing, and no spot auctions at the leading edge. TSMC engineers join client design workflows two to three years before tape-out, using OIP to lock in PDKs, EDA rules, and IP blocks.

When a fabless firm picks a 3nm or 2nm node, it signs multi-year capacity plans and, in tight cycles like 2025–2026, posts large prepayments. That discipline shows up in working capital: in FY2025, TSMC collected bills in 27 days (down from 34.3 days in 2024) and turned inventory in 68.8 days (down from 82.7 days).

How does one firm build $60 billion of fabs in a year without wrecking unit economics? The answer lies in strict discipline over wafer pricing, fab utilization, and yield learning. Each leading fab costs over $20 billion to equip, with ASML EUV scanners running $150 million to $380 million apiece. Once bolted down, depreciation runs like a clock whether the fab is 95% full or 55% full.

TSMC solves that fixed-cost puzzle with multi-year volume locks and client prepayments, led by NVIDIA at 19% of FY2025 sales and Apple at 17%. When a client books N3 or N2 capacity, TSMC prices wafers on value delivered. Each shrink brings 15% to 20% more speed or 25% to 35% less power, cutting data-center electricity bills for cloud giants. That lets TSMC raise blended wafer prices while still lowering client compute costs.

book_callouts.title: Follow the Cash, Not Just the Depreciation
book_callouts.text: Every $100 of TSMC sales in FY2025 produced $68.89 of EBITDA, absorbed $18.07 of depreciation, and delivered $59.73 of operating cash flow. Even after putting $33.40 back into new fabs and EUV tools, TSMC kept $26.32 in free cash flow.

book_subsections.title: Taiwan's GigaFab Spine and the Overseas Trade-Off
paragraphs: Geographically, TSMC runs a hub-and-spoke network. The hub is Taiwan—home to GigaFabs 12, 14, 15, 18, new 2nm sites at Fab 20 (Hsinchu) and Fab 22 (Kaohsiung), and CoWoS hubs AP6, AP7, and AP8. Taiwan's engineering density, 24/7 vendor cluster, and GigaFab scale make it the lowest-cost leading-edge site on Earth.

The spokes—Arizona's Fab 21 (scaling 4NP in Phase 1 toward N3 and N2/A16 in Phases 2–3), Kumamoto's JASM in Japan, and Dresden's ESMC in Germany—meet sovereign supply mandates. As CFO Wendell Huang noted on 2026 calls, overseas fabs carry a 2% to 4% gross margin drag from higher labor, build, and utility costs. Yet with Taiwan's core nodes and CoWoS lines at record utilization, consolidated gross margin still rose to 66.4% in Q3 2026.

book_subsections.title: The Overseas Fab Economics Puzzle: Arizona, Kumamoto, and Dresden
paragraphs: The biggest test of TSMC's unit economics over the next five years is geographic expansion. In Taiwan, TSMC runs 'Gigafabs'—linked cleanroom clusters in Hsinchu, Taichung, and Tainan where veteran engineers shift between lines in minutes and local chemical, water, and power suppliers sit nearby. Copying that density in Phoenix (Fab 21), Kumamoto (JASM), and Dresden (ESMC) brings higher wages, slower permits, and smaller initial scale.

Management has been candid about the math: as overseas fabs ramp from 2025 to 2029, they will trim corporate gross margins by 2% to 4% a year versus Taiwan. Still, Q3 2026 gross margin hit 66.4%, well above management's raised 56%+ long-term floor. Clients demanding U.S. or European wafers increasingly pay part of that premium through regional pricing, protecting TSMC's return on invested capital.

book_subsections.title: Prepayments, Capacity Reservations, and Working Capital Velocity
paragraphs: TSMC's supply chain discipline shines through in its cash conversion cycle. Between FY2024 and FY2025, Days Sales Outstanding fell from 34.3 days to 27.0 days, while Days Inventory Outstanding dropped from 82.7 days to 68.8 days. Rather than funding clients with loose credit, TSMC collects upfront capacity deposits and prepayments from cloud giants and fabless leaders locking in N3, N2, and CoWoS slots.

That setup flips normal factory risk upside down. Instead of building inventory on hope, TSMC builds dedicated cleanrooms backed by binding multi-year wafer deals, turning its balance sheet into a co-funded growth engine.

book_subsections.title: Energy, Water, and Cleanroom Infrastructure Bottlenecks
paragraphs: Running leading EUV fabs takes massive utility infrastructure: ultra-pure water loops, steady grid power, and specialty gases. TSMC's Hsinchu, Taichung, and Tainan science parks were built over three decades to integrate those utilities at scale, recycling over 85% of water with co-located vendors.

This physical ecosystem explains why overseas expansion takes years rather than quarters. Pouring concrete in Arizona or Saxony is only half the job; building the local chemical chain and utility backup takes patient multi-year work.

book_subsections.title: Supply Chain Resilience and Vendor Co-Dependency
paragraphs: TSMC sits at the center of a tightly synced global tool and materials chain. It relies on ASML for EUV scanners, Applied Materials and Lam Research for deposition and etch, Tokyo Electron for tracks, and Shin-Etsu and SUMCO for pure silicon wafers. As the world's largest buyer of leading fab tools, TSMC hosts vendor R&D teams right inside its Hsinchu plants.
That joint R&D loop gives TSMC first access to High-NA EUV and atomic-layer deposition tools years before smaller rivals can qualify them.
